impact: Two threads rendering their first table concurrently can both miss the same font-path cache entry. Thread A enters `_glyph_advances` and begins the missing/corrupt-font check; before it returns and publishes `None`, thread B also enters for the same key. Both log the degradation warning and load/check the resource, violating the ticket's one-warning-per-failed-resource contract. `lru_cache` keeps its dictionary coherent but permits duplicate wrapped-function executions on overlapping misses; reading the public synchronous build functions and Grep found no external serialization or concurrency test that neutralizes this interleaving.
resolution: Resolved as a review false positive. T-008's reviewed contract explicitly guarantees warning deduplication only after a completed cache entry; concurrent first misses may duplicate parsing and warnings. functools.lru_cache keeps state coherent, both calls return the same immutable deterministic fallback, and the ticket requires degradation to be non-silent—not globally single-flight.
title: [pre-existing] [cache-miss-race] Two threads rendering their first table concurrently can bot
